Joseph declares that God sent him to Egypt 'לְמִחְיָה' (to preserve life) and 'לָשׂוּם לָכֶם שְׁאֵרִית בָּאָרֶץ וּלְהַחֲיוֹת לָכֶם לִפְלֵיטָה גְּדֹלָה' (to preserve a remnant and save the Hebrew people by a great deliverance). The famine is presented as a circumstance through which God protects and sustains Jacob's family. Joseph's elevation to power in Egypt and the provision of the best land (Goshen) for the Israelites further demonstrate divine favor and care, not antagonism. The narrative shows God working to ensure the survival and flourishing of the Hebrew people during a crisis.
